newsitem.title: USA: NY Port Authority approves $2.9 billion budget.
newsitem.headline: NY Port Authority approves $2.9 billion budget.

text.p: The Port Authority of New York and New Jersey's board of commissioners said it approved a $2.9 billion budget for 1997 that cuts operating costs and delivers the largest one-year capital programme in the port's history.
The agency's service improvement programme includes allocating funds to re-open the Staten Island Rail Road.
This will restore direct rail freight service between New York and New Jersey, scheduled to re-open this year.
Port chairman Lewis Eisenberg said the board postponed action on the 1997 budget until late last week because new executive director, Robert Boyle, only took office on March 1.
The proposed budget includes $1.435 billion for operating expenses and $990 million for capital improvements, the highest capital spending in the agency's history.
Privatisation of the international arrivals terminal at John F. Kennedy International Airport will result in significant expenditure savings in this budget year, Boyle said.
Among the service improvements and capital projects approved are the following:
*A light-rail system for New York-JFK connecting all airport terminals with Jamaica Transportation Center and the Howard Beach subway. Construction to begin this year.
*Construction for a new ferry service to New York's Laguardia airport.
*Extension of Newark international airport's monorail connecting the Northeast Corridor lines with NJ Transit and Amtrak. Construction to begin this year.
*Installation of broadcast video services, providing news, weather and travel information to air passengers at all three airports.
